hook_text: Two instruments. Two units. Every day at eight.
clip_script: Rustenburg, North West. A Grade 5 class sets up a weather station. A white box on legs with slatted sides: a Stevenson screen, with a thermometer inside, measuring temperature in degrees Celsius, in the shade. A clear rain gauge in the open, measuring rain in millimetres. Every morning at eight, two learners read the instruments, write the numbers on a chart, and empty the gauge. That's how real weather records are made.
visual_style: Whiteboard white slatted box with a thermometer inside, then a rain gauge filling up, then numbers filling a chart.
mood: Curious and hands-on, like a science experiment.
pacing: Step by step, like following instructions.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make your own rain gauge from a plastic bottle.
